definitions.gloss: overthrowing one's superiors; the lower overthrowing the higher
definitions.explanation: A situation where those of lower rank overthrow or surpass those above them. Originally a historical term describing the social upheaval of Japan's Sengoku period, now used broadly for any upset where an underdog defeats a favorite.

examples.japanese: {下剋上|げこくじょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きた→起きる：00521_okiru⟧。
⟦{新人|しんじん}→新人：02500_shinjin⟧⟦チーム→チーム：03858_chiimu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{優勝|ゆうしょう}して→優勝する：25496_yuushousuru⟧{下剋上|げこくじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たした→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧。
examples.english: The rookie team won the championship and pulled off a major upset.

examples.japanese: ⟦{戦国時代|せんごくじだい}→戦国時代：19200_sengokujidai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{下剋上|げこくじょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれ→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧、⟦{家臣|かしん}→家臣：12655_kashin⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{主君|しゅくん}→主君：11712_shukun⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{倒|たお}す→倒す：01954_taosu⟧こと⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{珍|めずら}しくなかった→珍しい：01200_mezurashii⟧。
examples.english: The Sengoku period is called an era of gekokujou, and it was not unusual for vassals to overthrow their lords.

notes:
USAGE:
Originally a historical term describing the social phenomenon of the Sengoku period (15th-16th century) when lower-ranking warriors seized power from their superiors. In modern usage, it commonly describes upset victories in sports, business, or competitions.

FORMS:
{下|げ} (lower) + {剋|こく} (to overcome) + ⟦{上|じょう}→〜上：30365_jou⟧ (upper)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {下剋上|げこくじょう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{果|は}たす→果たす：10060_hatasu⟧: to achieve an upset
- {下剋上|げこくじょう}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{起|お}きる→起きる：00521_okiru⟧: an upset occurs
- {下剋上|げこくじょう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{時代|じだい}→時代：01424_jidai⟧: an era of upheaval
